Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
110 AM MST Thu Feb 26 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Unseasonably strong high pressure over the Desert Southwest will 
result in unusually warm conditions with afternoon highs approaching 
20 degrees above normal. 

- Multiple daily record highs and overnight warm lows are likely to 
be tied or broken through the weekend in Phoenix, Yuma, and El 
Centro.

&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Saturday/...
Strong subtropical high pressure continues to be sprawled across 
northern Mexico and the SW Conus with H5 heights analyzed in a 582-
585dm range across the forecast area. H8 temperatures have warmed 
within a few degrees of +20C yielding surface readings 15F-20F above 
normal and flirting with daily records. Model forecasts remain 
consistent depicting additional expansion and strengthening of the 
anti-cyclone over the next 48-72 hours with H5 heights reaching 
closer to 585-588dm, and low level thermal profiles continuing to 
warm placing both measures around the 99th percentile of late 
February climatology. Numerical guidance spreads remain extremely 
narrow providing unusually high confidence of record setting 
temperatures through the weekend (see Climate section). 

&&

.LONG TERM /Sunday through Wednesday/... 
The H5 high pressure ridge will start to become dampened early next 
week in response to incoming East Pacific shortwave energy, however 
height falls will be somewhat gradual to arrive with sfc-H8 
temperatures responding even slower. While guidance spread widens 
during this time frame, confidence is still excellent that high 
temperatures will be maintained 15F-20F above normal (and flirting 
with records) through Monday. Midlevel heights falls will become far 
more pronounced Tuesday as a closed cyclonic circulation propagates 
through northern Arizona. Despite this abrupt pattern change, 
thermal profiles will only be depressed slightly and the 
preponderance of model guidance suggests temperatures only 
retreating to around 10F above normal. Given the track of the 
shortwave and wind trajectories from the W/NW, moisture associated 
with this system should be extremely limited such that even higher 
elevation showers may be difficult to materialize. However, this 
wave will carve out a midlevel weakness and propensity for mean 
western Conus troughing with trailing Pacific shortwaves likely 
digging into the Great Basin and Southwest during the latter half of 
the week. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0520Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No aviation weather concerns under periods of FEW-SCT high cirrus 
cloud decks can be expected throughout the TAF period. The overall 
wind pattern will exhibit diurnal tendencies with periods of light 
variability. The overall speeds will remain under 10 kts. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
No aviation weather concerns under periods of FEW-SCT high cirrus 
cloud decks can be expected throughout the TAF period. Light west to 
northwest winds along with extended periods of light variability to 
even calm conditions can be expected. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Warm and dry weather will persist through early next week with 
temperatures reaching well above normal before cooling slightly 
towards the middle of the week. Minimum afternoon humidity levels 
will fall into the teens across the lower elevations, and only 
somewhat higher in foothills and mountains. This will follow mostly 
fair to good overnight recovery of 30-60% though some areas of poor 
recovery under 20% will exist. Wind speeds will largely remain under 
15 mph with modest afternoon upslope gusts 15-25 mph becoming 
common. Overall conditions will be favorable for early spring 
prescribed burning operations. 

&&
